speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a serious finding that requires immediate investigation. To begin narrowing down the cause, can you tell me exactly how old you are in days and when you first noticed the vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. 

Given the bilious vomiting in a newborn who is only six hours old, pyloric stenosis is clinically impossible as it typically presents at 3-6 weeks of age. The history of a sibling with pyloric stenosis and the immediate onset of symptoms strongly suggest a congenital obstruction like duodenal atresia. I am requesting an abdominal X-ray and an ultrasound to confirm the double-bubble sign and rule out other causes like malrotation. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray; REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound.
